A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the anisotropic diffusion properties of the human lung are not only present but also highly dependent on the field strength.

The main takeaway from our work is that
diffusion MRI can be used to characterize the regional orientation of lung airspaces in a noninvasive manner.
the diffusion anisotropy in the lung is not only dependent on the lung tissue structure, but also on the orientation of airspaces relative to the direction of diffusion.
diffusion anisotropy in the lung is a robust and repeatable measure of lung microstructure, and that it can be measured in a relatively short time using a single‐breath 3He diffusion MR protocol.
